newsitem.title: USA: Judge sends Waldholtz to jail for 37 months.
newsitem.headline: Judge sends Waldholtz to jail for 37 months.

text.p: A judge Thursday sentenced Joseph Waldholtz, the ex-husband of Utah Republican Representative Enid Greene, to 37 months in prison for fraud and other charges.

Greene showed up in the courtroom and wept quietly when the sentence was announced. She was ruined politically by the scandal when her husband admitted to mishandling more than $4 million borrowed from her family and others when he served as her campaign treasurer.
"I needed to be here today to end this chapter of my life.... "He is a very sick man ... I don't get any satisfaction from that (sentencing)," Greene said.
"This is a very sad day for me," she told reporters outside the courthouse, adding "it reflects the loss of the father of my child.

Waldholtz pleaded guilty to failing to report campaign contributions, making false statements to the federal election agency, causing his then-wife to file a false tax return in 1993 and bank fraud for a check-kiting scheme.

U.S. District Court Judge Norma Holloway Johnson dismissed Waldholtz's claims of regret as she sentenced him to 37 months, four more than the maximum sentence sought by the prosecutors under federal sentencing guidelines.
"You abused the public trust," she said, also scolding him for the damage he had done in defrauding family members and especially the impact on his young daughter, Elizabeth.

Because Waldholtz admitted at a hearing on Sept. 26 that he had continued to write bad checks, use heroin and other drugs, steal and misuse credit cards belonging to his family and friends, Johnson sentenced him to 37 months on one count, 12 months on another and 36 months on a third. But all will run concurrently, so he will serve a maximum of 37 months.

Prosecutor Craig Iscoe told reporters he was satisfied with the sentence and noted that Greene and others would not be prosecuted, partly because "Mr. Waldholtz has virtually no credibility" for a jury.

Waldholtz has been in jail since the Sept. 26 hearing when he claimed he was addicted to heroin and painkillers. His wife, once a rising star in the Republican Party, divorced him last year after he disappeared amidst a swirl of allegations of political and financial misdeeds.
She said she would take time off when her term ends in January to decide what to do next.

Iscoe told Holloway in September that Waldholtz claimed he was using a gram of heroin a day and that he forged his dentist father's signature to obtain painkillers, stole checks from his stepmother and wrote $39,600 of checks on an account in which he kept an average balance of $60.

Waldholtz stole credit cards from his father, Harvey, and a friend and used them for unauthorised purchases. He stole his friend's Mastercard from her purse while she was being treated by his father, Iscoe said.
His father and his wife kicked him out of their Squirrel Hill, Pennsylvania home and changed the locks.

Greene, who won office as a champion of family values, got a divorce on June 5, the same day that Waldholtz pleaded guilty, and has sole custody of their year-old daughter. She has maintained that Waldholtz duped her but she decided not to seek re-election this month.
